full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J:- The Rule issued calling upon the Opposite Party No. 1 to show cause as, to why the impugned judgment and order dated 19.09.2005 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Court No. 08, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 10 of 2003 (Arising out of Title Appeal No. 381 of 1992) should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders be passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite party no. I as plaintiff filed a suit for declaration of title in respect of the suit land being Title Suit No.35 of 1980 in the 4ui Court of Additional Assistant Judge, Dhaka against the present petitioner. The learned Assistant Judge after hearing, the parties decreed the suit. Being aggrieved the defendant petitioner filed a Title Appeal being No. 381 of 1992 in the Court of learned District Judge, Dhaka which was heard and disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge, 8th Court, Dhaka. It is the case of the present petitioner that on 08.09.2003 the learned advocate for the petitioner was on his leg in another court but the learned appellate court dismissed the appeal for default. Thereafter, an application was filed under Order 41 Rule 19 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In that miscellaneous case I 9.09.2005 was a date for hearing but on that date the petitioner filed an application for adjournment on the ground of illness of his advocate. But the learned Additional District Judge did not allow the application and dismissed the miscellaneous case vide the impugned order dated 19.09.2005. 

 5. The learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that during pendency of the miscellaneous case being no. 10 of 2003 an application was filed on behalf of the defendant appellant-petitioners on the ground of illness of their learned advocate. But the learned appellate Court without considering the ground rejected the same and dismissed the miscellaneous case for default. The learned advocate further submits that the learned Additional District Judge committed illegality in not considering the adjournment application of the defendant-appellant-petitioners and thereby committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 6. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioners the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondent-opposite parties opposing the Rule submits that the revisional application as it was instituted is not maintainable in the eye of law and there is no scope to entertain such application under Section 115 (4) of the Code of Civil Procedure against the order dated 19.09.2005 passed in miscellaneous case no. 10 of 2003 arising out of Title Appeal No. 381 of 1992 since the miscellaneous case being no. 10 of 2003 was under the provisions laid down in Order 41 Rule 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned advocate further submits that the order is not revisional rather appeal able under Order 43 Rule Ill) of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned advocate in this regard pointed out the relevant provisions of law. 

 8. On perusal of the case record it transpires that the present plaintiff-respondent-opposite party initially filed a declaratory suit in the 4th Additional Court of learned Assistant Judge, Dhaka against the present defendant-petitioners and in that suit the plaintiff obtained a decree. Against that judgment and decree the defendant-appellant-petitioners filed a Title Appeal being No. 381 of 1992 in the Court of learned District Judge, Dhaka which was dismissed for default by the learned Additional District Judge, 8th Court, Dhaka. Thereafter, an application was filed under Order XLI Rule 19 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for re-admission of the appeal and hearing the same which was also dismissed for default by the impugned order dated 19.09.2005. 

 9. It is apparent from the face of the papers that the Miscellaneous Case being No, 10 of 2003 arising out of an application filed under Order XL I Rule 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure which was fixed for hearing on 19.09.2005. On the very date the petitioners filed an adjournment application and the learned Additional District Judge, 8th Court, Dhaka rejected the same. Subsequently by the selfsame order the learned court dismissed the case for default. Therefore obviously the impugned order was passed on an application filed tinder Order XLI Rule 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure which is an appealable order under the ambit of Order XLIII Rule 1(t) of the Code of Civil Procedure.
